title: Count Distinct Vowels in a String
statement:
You are given a string `s`. Count how many **distinct vowels** it contains and print that number.

The vowels are `a`, `e`, `i`, `o` and `u`. Matching is case-insensitive, so `A` and `a` are the same vowel. A vowel is counted once no matter how many times it appears, and the letter `y` is not a vowel. Every other character (consonants, digits, spaces, punctuation) is ignored.

The answer is therefore an integer between `0` and `5`.
inputFormat: A single line containing the string `s` (it may contain spaces).
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the number of distinct vowels in `s`.
constraints: s consists of printable ASCII characters (codes 32 to 126)
s contains at least one character that is not a space

examples.explanation: The only vowels appearing are `i` and `e` (the capital `E` counts as `e`), so the answer is 2 even though they occur many times.
The vowels `e`, `u`, `a`, `i` and `o` all occur, so all five distinct vowels are present.
There are no vowels: `y` does not count, and digits and spaces are ignored.

hints: Convert each character to lower case before deciding whether it is a vowel.
Remember which vowels you have already seen; a set of at most five letters (or five boolean flags) is enough.
The answer is the size of that set after scanning the whole string. You can stop early once all five have been seen.
